aggregate_documents.description: Add up or average a numeric field across the matching documents, without reading them.
aggregate_documents.name: aggregate_documents

parameters.description: The collection to work in. Pick a root collection, or type a path to reach a subcollection - 'users' or 'users/alice/pets'. A collection path always has an odd number of segments.
parameters.name: collection

parameters.description: Which calculation to run over the matches.
parameters.name: aggregation

parameters.description: The numeric field to add up or average. Not needed when counting. Documents where the field is missing or is not a number are skipped.
parameters.name: field_name

parameters.description: Which documents to match. Each filter is a field, an operator and a value - for example {"field": "status", "operator": "EQUAL", "value": "open"}. The four IS_NULL/IS_NOT_NULL/IS_NAN/IS_NOT_NAN operators test the field on their own and take no value; IN, NOT_IN and ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY take a list. Leave empty to match every document. Filtering or sorting on more than one field needs a composite index - Firestore's error carries a link that creates it.
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Whether a document has to match every filter or just one.
parameters.name: combine_filters

parameters.description: Search every collection with this id anywhere in the database, not just the one at this path - Firestore calls it a collection group query. Use it to read, say, every 'comments' subcollection under every post at once.
parameters.display_name: Include subcollections with the same name
parameters.name: include_subcollections

append_to_array.description: Add values to an array on a document, skipping any already there, so running the step twice does not duplicate an entry.
